elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, consolidation/acquisition
elements.evidence: "or a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition"

elements.element: Customer consent-free assignment extends to sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "IBM will not assign this Agreement ... without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and will not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: Neither the original nor the redlined clause creates any IBM termination right on Customer change of control; condition demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Customer carve-out for successors; IBM may assign with consent "not to be unreasonably withheld"
No notice mechanic appears; clause is silent on notice.

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld" (both directions)

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully met: the Customer carve-out now covers affiliates and sale of substantially all assets, and one inserted sentence subjects IBM's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a competitor.
No Vendor change-of-control termination right exists anywhere in the clause, so that conditional preferred element is satisfied by absence.

Edits are confined to one phrase replacement plus a single reciprocal sentence; the void-assignment and continuing-liability sentences and all other commercial terms remain intact, with no undefined term or dangling mechanic introduced.
Fallback is not independently complete only because no written-notice mechanic is added, which is irrelevant given the preferred level is achieved.
